parts:
Hi,

Can you check the actual number of rows in the variables given to the failing inla.stack call?  Since you supply (A,1) for the A matrices, it tries to infer the required size of the second A matrix, and apparently that doesn’t match your other inputs, either the effect or response variable.

Also, even though the error occurs in inla.stack, are you supplying the needed 2 column matrix input needed for a 2-likelihood model?

You say the error happens when you run INLA(), but the error looks like it comes from inla.stack(). Can you supply the output from
  traceback()
when run after the error message appears?

Finn

Finn
